title: Bell Canada says 'agentic' threat actor stole enterprise customer data
date_note: Date of the incident as stated in Bell's statement to BleepingComputer; the article was published 20 November.
geo_basis: country; the article gives no city
summary: Bell told BleepingComputer that an agentic threat actor accessed some of its systems on 17 November, including one used to order and provision circuits, and exfiltrated some enterprise customer data. A customer notification describes a pre-production Maximo environment and lists business contact details, ticket titles and some IP addresses. Bell says it contained the incident, reports no impact to customer services and does not know the attribution.
plain: Bell Canada says an attacker it calls 'agentic' took some business customer data from a system used to order network circuits. Bell says services were not affected.
exec: A major telecom confirmed enterprise customer data was taken from a circuit-ordering system; Bell says customer services were not affected.
action: Enterprise customers of Bell: follow Bell's notification, watch for unsolicited requests and social engineering impersonating Bell, and use the IOCs Bell is sharing with customers and the CCCS.
impact: Some enterprise customer data exfiltrated; Bell reports no impact to customer services.

sources.name: BleepingComputer: Bell Canada says 'agentic' hacker stole enterprise customer data

validation.note: BleepingComputer quotes Bell's own statement and a Bell customer notification; no second publisher read. Bell's statement and notification themselves were not linked or read.
